label: Active Directory
summary: A Windows domain over LDAP, read-only: domain controllers and FSMO roles, privileged group members, password policy, and security findings such as Kerberos-roastable accounts, unconstrained delegation or an old krbtgt password.

credentials.label: Service account
credentials.help: A plain domain user created for DumbMonit, member of no group.

fields.label: User name
fields.help: The user principal name (svc-dumbmonit@corp.example.com), DOMAIN\svc-dumbmonit, or the full DN.

fields.label: Password
fields.help: Stored encrypted, never shown again.

setup.title: Create a read-only service account for DumbMonit
steps:
Active Directory Users and Computers → your domain → Users → New → User: name it as follows, set a long random password and add it to no group.
svc-dumbmonit
On its Account tab, tick Password never expires, or the bind fails the day the password does.

Optional, to see inbound replication status: grant the account the right listed below on the domain object.
dsacls "DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com" /G "CORP\svc-dumbmonit:CA;Monitor active directory replication"
For LDAPS, export your certification authority's certificate as Base-64 encoded X.509 and paste it as CA certificate below.
In DumbMonit, enter a domain controller's name as its certificate names it (dc1.corp.example.com) and log in as svc-dumbmonit@corp.example.com.

ports.purpose: LDAPS (default), also to the other domain controllers
Only with the StartTLS or plain LDAP option
Only with the DNS servers option
Only with the DNS servers option

permissions:
Domain Users membership only
No group or delegation is needed to read

Monitor active directory replication
Optional: inbound replication status
setup.warning: Plain LDAP on port 389 sends the password in clear and is refused by default: use LDAPS, or StartTLS on port 389.

options.label: Connection security
options.help: ldaps (port 636) encrypts from the first byte; starttls upgrades port 389 before logging in; plain sends the password in clear text and needs Allow plain LDAP.

options.label: Port
options.help: Used if the address does not give a port: 636 for LDAPS, 389 otherwise.

options.label: CA certificate
options.help: The PEM certificate (Base-64 encoded X.509) of the authority that issued the domain controllers' certificates. Only that authority is then trusted.

options.label: Accept an unverifiable certificate
options.help: Skips every certificate check: the connection stays encrypted, but anyone on the path could pose as the domain controller. Prefer the CA certificate above.

options.label: Allow plain LDAP
options.help: Required for the plain setting: the service account's password then crosses the network readable by anyone on the path.

options.label: DNS servers
options.help: Optional. IP addresses of the DNS servers that know the domain (comma-separated). Every name lookup of this monitor then goes through them instead of the system resolver; empty keeps the system DNS.

options.label: Check every domain controller
options.help: Opens a connection to the LDAP port of each domain controller of the domain, to alert when one stops answering. Names that do not resolve from DumbMonit are reported, not alerted on.

options.label: Inactive user after (days)
options.help: An enabled user with no logon for this long is counted as inactive. The last-logon date can lag by up to 14 days.

options.label: Inactive computer after (days)
options.help: An enabled computer with no logon for this long is counted as inactive.

options.label: Full inventory every (minutes)
options.help: Every user and computer is read in the background at this pace (1 to 1440); health is read at every check.

options.label: Timeout (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each LDAP operation, from 1 to 60.

label: AdGuard Home
summary: The DNS filter: protection on or paused, queries and blocks, filter lists that stopped updating, upstream servers that fail, updates.
examples: AdGuard Home on OpenWrt or a NAS

credentials.label: User name / password
credentials.help: The dedicated user added to AdGuardHome.yaml, sent as HTTP basic authentication.

credentials.label: No authentication
credentials.help: Only for an AdGuard Home with no user at all in AdGuardHome.yaml.

setup.title: Add a user for DumbMonit to AdGuard Home
steps:
Make a bcrypt hash of a long random password (htpasswd comes with apache2-utils or httpd-tools).
htpasswd -B -C 10 -n -b dumbmonit 'LONG-RANDOM-PASSWORD'

Stop AdGuard Home, add this line under users: in AdGuardHome.yaml with HASH replaced by the printed hash, then start it again.
- { name: dumbmonit, password: "HASH" }
In DumbMonit, enter the address of the AdGuard Home web interface, then the user dumbmonit and its password.

ports.purpose: Only with the web interface left on port 3000, the first-run default
Only with the https scheme option

setup.warning: AdGuard Home has no read-only user, so dumbmonit can change every setting: keep its password to DumbMonit alone, and turn on HTTPS in Settings → Encryption settings across an untrusted network.

options.label: Protocol
options.help: AdGuard Home serves its web interface over plain HTTP until you give it a certificate in Settings → Encryption settings. HTTPS then.

options.label: Port
options.help: The web interface port chosen during setup. Used if the address does not give a port.

options.label: Accept an unverifiable certificate
options.help: For a self-signed or private certificate: enable this if the connection is refused for that reason.

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call, from 1 to 60.

options.label: Test upstream servers
options.help: Asks AdGuard Home to test each upstream DNS server at every check, as its Test upstreams button does. An upstream that fails or stays silent for 4 seconds is reported down.

label: Server with agent
summary: Linux, Windows, macOS or FreeBSD: CPU, memory, disks, network, Docker, services, backups.

credentials.label: No authentication
credentials.help: Nothing is sent: the monitor answers without credentials.

setup.title: Install the agent on the machine
steps: In DumbMonit, add a monitor and pick Server with the agent, then choose how the machine reaches the server: directly, or through the relay of a remote site behind a firewall.
An enrollment token (dmon_…) is shown once, with the install command ready to copy for Linux/macOS, Windows and Docker.
Run that install command on the machine, with elevated rights (sudo on Linux and macOS, an elevated PowerShell on Windows).
The page waits for the first report (a few seconds), then lets you name the machine, file it in a folder and place it at a site, on the spot.

Optional, for Docker: if the agent runs under a dedicated user, add that user to the "docker" group and restart the agent.
usermod -aG docker dumbmonit
For a fleet (a playbook, a machine image), tick Several machines with this command; a whole Windows domain goes through the Active Directory kit, offered on the same page.

ports.purpose: Readings and commands (default port, 443 behind a TLS proxy)

setup.warning: The agent contacts the server, never the other way round: no port needs to be opened on the monitored machine.

label: Service found by an agent
summary: Docker, backups, ZFS, VMs or tunnels found by the agent on a machine, each watched as its own device.

credentials.label: No authentication
credentials.help: Nothing is sent: the monitor answers without credentials.

setup.title: Created by the agent
steps: Install the agent on the machine: each service it finds becomes a monitor under that machine on its first report.
To stop watching one, untick it in the machine's "Services found by the agent" panel or delete its monitor.

ports.purpose: Readings and commands (default port, 443 behind a TLS proxy)

setup.warning: If the machine stops reporting, its services are shown as hidden behind it rather than raising alerts of their own.

label: Apache httpd
summary: The web server: busy and idle workers, the worker scoreboard by state, and request/byte rates when ExtendedStatus is on.

credentials.label: No password
credentials.help: The status page is filtered so that only the DumbMonit host reaches it.

credentials.label: Basic auth
credentials.help: If the status page sits behind a basic auth block or directive.

setup.title: Enable Apache's mod_status
steps:
Enable mod_status (it ships with Apache and is usually on already).
a2enmod status

Add this location to the Apache configuration, restricted to the DumbMonit host (adjust the address).
<Location "/server-status">
SetHandler server-status
Require ip 10.0.0.5
</Location>

Optional: turn on the request and byte counters.
ExtendedStatus On

Reload Apache, then open http://apache.lan/server-status?auto from the DumbMonit host.
apachectl graceful
In DumbMonit, enter the Apache host, for example apache.lan, and the path if it is not /server-status.

ports.purpose: Only if the status page is served over HTTPS

setup.warning: Without ExtendedStatus, requests and bytes are not reported at all: the chart stays empty rather than flat.

options.label: Protocol
options.help: The status page listens over plain HTTP unless Apache gave it TLS.

options.label: Port
options.help: Used if the address does not give a port.

options.label: Status path
options.help: Location where "SetHandler server-status" was declared, without the "?auto" query string: it is added automatically.

options.label: Accept an unverifiable certificate
options.help: For a reverse proxy with a self-signed or private certificate: enable this if the connection is refused for that reason.

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call, from 1 to 120.

label: Aruba Central
summary: Beta. The Wi-Fi access points, switches and gateways of an HPE Aruba Networking Central account through its cloud API: devices offline, active critical alerts, devices in poor health, and the number of connected clients.

credentials.label: API client
credentials.help: Recommended: DumbMonit exchanges the client for an access token and renews it by itself.

fields.label: Client ID
fields.help: The client ID of the personal API client created in step 2.

fields.label: Client secret
fields.help: Shown once when the client is created. Stored encrypted, never shown again.

credentials.label: Access token
credentials.help: Works for a test, but expires after two hours and DumbMonit cannot renew it.

fields.label: Access token
fields.help: An access token of your Central instance. Stored encrypted, never shown again.

setup.title: Create a personal API client for DumbMonit
steps: Sign in to HPE GreenLake (common.cloud.hpe.com) and open Manage Workspace → Personal API clients.

Click Create personal API client, name it as follows and choose your Central instance as the service.
dumbmonit
Copy the client ID and the client secret: the secret is shown once, and HPE keeps no copy.
In Central, open the API gateway page (Menu → API Gateway → REST API) and note the base URL of your region.
In DumbMonit, enter that base URL as the address (for example us1.api.central.arubanetworks.com) and paste the client ID and the client secret.

ports.purpose: Central API (HTTPS, the base URL of your region)

permissions:
Read access to Central monitoring
Devices, alerts and health overviews: DumbMonit never changes anything
setup.warning: Beta: written from HPE's published API reference, not yet tested on a real Central account. It reads the new Central API with Central credentials; credentials scoped to the GreenLake platform and classic Central are not supported.

options.label: Sign-in host
options.help: The HPE GreenLake host that issues the access tokens. Change it only if HPE gives you another.

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call, from 1 to 120.

label: authentik (beta)
summary: Readiness, workers, failed system tasks, outpost connections, version updates, users.

credentials.label: API token
credentials.help: The key of an API token created for a service account, sent as "Authorization: Bearer …".

fields.label: API token
fields.help: Stored encrypted, never shown again.

setup.title: Create an API token in authentik
steps:
In authentik, open Directory → Users → Create a service account and name it as follows, without a random password.
dumbmonit
Put that user in a group that can open the authentik interface, so it can read the system pages.
Open Directory → Tokens and App passwords, create a token for that user with the intent API Token and no expiry, and copy its key.
In DumbMonit, enter authentik's address and paste the key.

ports.purpose: Only with the https scheme on authentik's own HTTPS port
Only with the https scheme behind a reverse proxy

setup.warning: authentik has no read-only role for its system pages: the token's user must be allowed into the interface, so keep the key only in DumbMonit. Pages the token cannot read are skipped, not failed.

options.label: Protocol
options.help: Used when the address does not start with http:// or https://.

options.label: Port
options.help: Used if the address does not give a port. Choosing the other protocol without a port uses 80 or 443.

options.label: Accept an unverifiable certificate
options.help: For a self-signed or private certificate: enable this if the connection is refused for that reason.

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call, from 1 to 120. Photo and file counts are computed on every call on a large instance.

label: AWS (CloudWatch)
summary: CloudWatch alarms in the ALARM state, EC2 status checks and CPU, and RDS CPU and free storage.

credentials.label: Access key
credentials.help: Access key ID and secret access key of a read-only IAM user (or of a user allowed to assume a read-only role).

fields.label: Access key ID
fields.help: Starts with AKIA for a long-term key.

fields.label: Secret access key
fields.help: Shown once when the access key is created.

setup.title: Create a read-only IAM user for DumbMonit
steps:
In the AWS console, open IAM, Policies, Create policy, JSON tab, paste this read-only policy and name it DumbMonitReadOnly.
{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms","cloudwatch:ListMetrics","cloudwatch:GetMetricData"],"Resource":"*"}]}
Open IAM, Users, Create user: name it dumbmonit, leave console access off, and attach the DumbMonitReadOnly policy.
Open the user, Security credentials, Create access key, choose Application running outside AWS. Copy the access key ID and the secret access key: the secret is shown once.
Optional, to use a role instead: attach the policy to a role that trusts the user, give the user only sts:AssumeRole on that role, and copy the role ARN into the Role ARN option.
In DumbMonit, enter monitoring.<region>.amazonaws.com as the address, paste the key and its secret, and set the same region in the Region option.

ports.purpose: Only with a role ARN: STS AssumeRole (HTTPS, sts.<region>.amazonaws.com)

permissions:
cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms
Lists the alarms in the ALARM state; changes nothing.

cloudwatch:ListMetrics
Finds the EC2 instances and RDS databases that publish metrics.

cloudwatch:GetMetricData
Reads CPU, status checks, free storage and connections over the last 10 minutes.

sts:AssumeRole (only with a role ARN)
Lets the user assume the read-only role; allow it on that role only.
setup.warning: Use a dedicated IAM user with only these read permissions, never a key that can change resources. AWS bills GetMetricData per metric requested (USD 0.01 per 1,000): a long check interval keeps the cost low on large accounts.

options.label: Region
options.help: AWS region of the account resources, also used to sign requests. It must match the region in the address.

options.label: Role ARN
options.help: Optional. Role to assume through STS, instead of reading with the user's own permissions.

options.label: STS endpoint URL
options.help: Optional, only with a role. Replaces https://sts.<region>.amazonaws.com (VPC endpoint, China or GovCloud regions).

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call, from 1 to 120.

label: Microsoft Azure
summary: Resource Health and active Azure Monitor alerts of an Azure subscription, read through a Reader service principal.

credentials.label: Entra application (service principal)
credentials.help: The client ID and a client secret of an Entra application that has the Reader role on the subscription.

fields.label: Application (client) ID
fields.help: The Application (client) ID of the app registration, a GUID.

fields.label: Client secret
fields.help: The Value of a client secret of the app registration (shown once when created).

setup.title: Create a read-only application for DumbMonit
steps: In the Azure portal, open Microsoft Entra ID > App registrations > New registration, name it DumbMonit, keep single tenant, then Register.
On the Overview page, copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID.
Open Certificates & secrets > New client secret, choose a lifetime, then copy the secret Value: it is shown once.
Open Subscriptions > your subscription > Access control (IAM) > Add > Add role assignment, pick the Reader role, select the DumbMonit application, then Review + assign.
Copy the Subscription ID from the subscription Overview page.
In DumbMonit, enter management.azure.com as address, paste the client ID and secret, and fill the Tenant ID and Subscription ID options.
permissions:
Reader (role on the subscription)
Reads Resource Health and the active Azure Monitor alerts; changes nothing.
setup.warning: A stopped or deallocated virtual machine is reported by Azure as unavailable on the user's request: it is counted apart and raises no alert. Azure Monitor alerts need the Microsoft.AlertsManagement resource provider registered on the subscription; without it only Resource Health is monitored.

options.label: Tenant ID
options.help: The Directory (tenant) ID of the application, a GUID or a domain such as contoso.onmicrosoft.com.

options.label: Subscription ID
options.help: The subscription to watch, as shown on its Overview page in the Azure portal.

options.label: Sign-in URL
options.help: Where the access token is requested. Change it only for a sovereign cloud, such as https://login.microsoftonline.us.

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call, from 1 to 120.

label: Caddy
summary: The web server and reverse proxy: upstreams failing their health checks, a configuration reload that failed, handler errors and the share of 5xx answers.

credentials.label: Read-only view
credentials.help: The user of the basic_auth block of the read-only view (recommended).

credentials.label: No password
credentials.help: The admin API itself, reachable only by the DumbMonit host.

setup.title: Publish a read-only view of Caddy's admin API
steps:
Hash a password for the user dumbmonit.
caddy hash-password --plaintext 'a-long-password'

Optional: add metrics to the global options block at the top of the Caddyfile to count requests and errors.
metrics
Filter port 2020 so that only the DumbMonit host reaches it.
In DumbMonit, enter the Caddy host with that port, for example caddy.lan:2020, and the user dumbmonit with its password.
permissions:
GET on /config/apps/http/servers
Servers and routes

GET on /reverse_proxy/upstreams
Upstream health

GET on /metrics
Request counters (optional)
setup.warning: Never expose the admin API itself: whoever reaches port 2019 can replace the configuration or stop Caddy.

options.help: The admin API and the read-only view listen over plain HTTP unless you gave them TLS.

options.help: Used if the address does not give a port: 2019 for the admin API itself.

label: Ceph
summary: Beta. A Ceph cluster through the REST API of the manager's dashboard: health and its checks, OSDs down or nearly full, placement groups not clean, capacity, pools, monitors out of the quorum.

credentials.label: Dashboard user and password
credentials.help: The dumbmonit user of the Ceph dashboard, with the read-only role.

fields.label: User name
fields.help: The dashboard user created for DumbMonit.

setup.title: Create a read-only dashboard user for DumbMonit
steps:
Check that the dashboard is enabled and note the address of the active manager.
ceph mgr services

Write a long random password to a file, and keep it: DumbMonit needs it.
openssl rand -base64 24 | tr -d '\n' | tee /tmp/dumbmonit.pwd

Create the user with the built-in read-only role.
ceph dashboard ac-user-create dumbmonit -i /tmp/dumbmonit.pwd read-only

Delete the password file.
shred -u /tmp/dumbmonit.pwd
In DumbMonit, enter the address of the active manager (for example ceph.lan) with that user name and password.

ports.purpose: Only with the HTTP protocol option

permissions:
read-only role
Reads the state of the cluster, changes nothing
setup.warning: A standby manager redirects to the active one: use the address of the active manager. The dashboard ships a self-signed certificate: tick "Accept an unverifiable certificate" unless you installed your own.

options.label: Protocol
options.help: Used when the address does not start with http:// or https://.

options.label: Port
options.help: Used if the address does not give a port: the dashboard port, 8443 over HTTPS and 8080 over HTTP.

options.label: Accept an unverifiable certificate
options.help: The device ships a self-signed certificate: enable this unless you installed one DumbMonit trusts.

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call, from 1 to 120.

label: Cloudflare
summary: Zones, tunnels, certificates, traffic errors and load balancer pools of a Cloudflare account, read through the Cloudflare API.

credentials.label: API token
credentials.help: A Cloudflare API token with read-only permissions.

fields.label: API token
fields.help: The token created in the dashboard, shown once.

setup.title: Create a read-only API token for DumbMonit
steps: In the Cloudflare dashboard, open My Profile > API Tokens > Create Token > Create Custom Token, and name it DumbMonit.
Add the read-only permissions listed below, and nothing else. The first one is required; the others switch on one part each.
Under Account Resources and Zone Resources, choose the account and the zones to monitor (All zones is fine).
Click Continue to summary > Create Token, then copy the token: it is shown once.

In DumbMonit, use this address and paste the token as API token. Leave Account ID empty unless the token covers several accounts.
api.cloudflare.com
permissions:
Zone > Zone > Read
Lists the zones and their status; required.

Zone > SSL and Certificates > Read
Reads the expiry date of the certificates of each zone.

Zone > Analytics > Read
Reads the requests and 5xx responses of each zone.

Zone > Load Balancers > Read
Lists the load balancers of each zone.

Account > Cloudflare Tunnel > Read
Reads the status of the tunnels.

Account > Account Settings > Read
Finds the account of the tunnels; not needed if the Account ID option is filled.

Account > Load Balancing: Monitors And Pools > Read
Reads the health of the load balancer pools.
setup.warning: A part whose permission is missing (or that the plan does not include) is skipped and its readable metric is 0; it does not make the monitor fail. Only the zones the token can see are watched.

options.label: Account ID
options.help: The Cloudflare account of the tunnels and load balancer pools. Empty: read from the token (up to 5 accounts).

options.label: Read traffic
options.help: Read requests and 5xx responses of each zone (one GraphQL call per 10 zones). Turn off to save API calls.

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call, from 1 to 120.

label: CrowdSec
summary: The security engine: active decisions, alerts, bouncers that stopped pulling, log lines read and not parsed, Local API health.

credentials.label: Metrics only
credentials.help: Reads /metrics, and /health of the Local API. Nothing to create.

credentials.label: Bouncer API key
credentials.help: Also proves the Local API answers decision queries. A bouncer key can only read decisions.

fields.label: Bouncer API key
fields.help: Shown once by cscli bouncers add. Stored encrypted, never shown again.

credentials.label: Machine login
credentials.help: Also reads the alerts of the last 24 hours, counted by country for the threat map. Addresses are never kept.

fields.label: Machine name
fields.help: The name given to cscli machines add.

fields.label: Password
fields.help: The password given to cscli machines add. Stored encrypted, never shown again.

setup.title: Let DumbMonit read CrowdSec's metrics
steps:
Make the metrics reachable: set listen_addr in the prometheus section of /etc/crowdsec/config.yaml to an address DumbMonit can reach, then restart CrowdSec.
sudo sed -i 's/listen_addr: 127.0.0.1/listen_addr: 0.0.0.0/' /etc/crowdsec/config.yaml
sudo systemctl restart crowdsec

Check from the DumbMonit host that the metrics answer on port 6060, and filter that port so only the DumbMonit host reaches it.
curl -s http://crowdsec.lan:6060/metrics | grep cs_info
DumbMonit also checks the Local API on port 8080 of the same host: untick Check the Local API for a host that only runs an agent.

Optional: create a bouncer key and paste it as Bouncer API key below.
sudo cscli bouncers add dumbmonit

Or, for the threat map of the Security page: create a machine login and choose Machine login below. Only the country of each alert is kept.
sudo cscli machines add dumbmonit --password 'a-long-password'
In DumbMonit, enter the CrowdSec host, for example "crowdsec.lan".

ports.purpose: Only with the Local API check option (on by default)

permissions:
Bouncer API key (optional)
Read-only: it can only read decisions

Machine login (optional)
Reads the alerts; a machine can also send alerts, so keep it for DumbMonit only
setup.warning: A bouncer that stops pulling keeps enforcing a frozen list: DumbMonit warns when a bouncer's requests stop for 30 minutes.

options.help: These servers listen over plain HTTP unless you put them behind a reverse proxy with TLS. HTTPS then.

options.help: The prometheus listen_port of CrowdSec.

options.help: Checks /health of the Local API on this host. Untick for a host that only runs an agent.

label: Domain name (DNS)
summary: A name resolves, and points to the address you expect.
examples: An internal name served by your Pi-hole or AdGuard

credentials.label: No authentication
credentials.help: Nothing is sent: the monitor answers without credentials.

setup.title: Monitor a DNS resolution
steps: In the address, write the name to resolve, without "http://": "www.example.com".
Pick another record type in the options if you do not want an IPv4 address (A record).
To monitor your own DNS server, enter its IP address in "DNS server to query".
To detect hijacking, list the addresses the answer must contain in "Expected values".

ports.purpose: DNS query too large for UDP (default port)

setup.warning: Give the DNS server by its IP address, not by a name.

options.label: Record type
options.help: A for an IPv4 address, AAAA for IPv6, MX for mail, CNAME for an alias…

options.label: DNS server to query
options.help: IP address of a resolver, port optional. Empty: the system resolver. Handy to check your own DNS server.

options.label: Expected values
options.help: Values that must all appear in the answer, separated by commas. Empty: only the resolution is checked.

options.label: Comparison
options.help: "contains": each expected value must appear somewhere in the answer. "exact": the answer must hold those values and nothing else, so a record added beside the right one fails the check.

options.label: Forbidden values
options.help: Values that must never appear in the answer, separated by commas: a former host's address, an expired validation record. Checked before the expected ones.

options.label: Alert when the answer changes
options.help: Records a fingerprint of the sorted answer and alerts whenever it changes, without having to write the expected values. Leave off for names whose answer rotates between servers (large round-robin pools, geographic DNS).

options.label: Timeout (seconds)
options.help: Time after which the service is reported down if it has not answered. Between 1 and 60.

label: Domain expiry
summary: A registered domain, read from its registry over RDAP: days left before expiry, a hold that takes it out of the DNS, a redemption period, and its registrar.
examples: The domain of your mail server

credentials.label: No authentication
credentials.help: Nothing is sent: the monitor answers without credentials.

setup.title: Watch a domain's registration
steps: Enter the registered domain, for example "example.com", not a name under it such as www.example.com.

For an extension the IANA does not list, such as .ch, set "RDAP server" to the registry's address.
https://rdap.nic.ch/

ports.purpose: RDAP query to the registry and to the IANA (HTTPS)

setup.warning: A domain in clientHold or serverHold is taken out of the DNS: every site and mailbox under it stops.

options.label: RDAP server
options.help: The RDAP address of the registry, for an extension the IANA does not list. Empty: found in the IANA bootstrap file.

options.label: Refresh interval (hours)
options.help: How often the registry is asked, from 1 to 168. The days left are recomputed at every check in between.

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call to IANA or to the registry, from 1 to 120.

summary: Made-up measurements, to explore DumbMonit without any hardware.

setup.title: Create a read-only service account for DumbMonit
steps:
Create the service account.
kubectl create serviceaccount dumbmonit -n kube-system

Create a ClusterRole that can only get and list what DumbMonit reads.
kubectl create clusterrole dumbmonit-read --verb=get,list --resource=nodes,pods,persistentvolumeclaims,events,deployments.apps,statefulsets.apps,daemonsets.apps

Bind the role to the service account.
kubectl create clusterrolebinding dumbmonit-read --clusterrole=dumbmonit-read --serviceaccount=kube-system:dumbmonit

Create a token that does not expire, then print the token and the cluster CA in base64.
echo '{"apiVersion":"v1","kind":"Secret","metadata":{"name":"dumbmonit-token","namespace":"kube-system","annotations":{"kubernetes.io/service-account.name":"dumbmonit"}},"type":"kubernetes.io/service-account-token"}' | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n kube-system get secret dumbmonit-token -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d
kubectl -n kube-system get secret dumbmonit-token -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}'
In DumbMonit, enter the API server address (for example https://k3s.lan:6443), paste the token as Service account token and the CA as Cluster CA certificate.

setup.title: Install the agent on the MDaemon server, then add this monitor
steps: On the Windows server that runs MDaemon, add a Server with agent monitor in DumbMonit and run its PowerShell command in an elevated PowerShell. The agent finds MDaemon by itself.
Back here, enter the server address and choose that agent in Agent installed on this server. DumbMonit pre-selects the one with the same host name.
Leave the credential on Services only: the agent already brings the queues, sessions, Windows services and disk space, and the mail ports are checked from DumbMonit.

Optional, only to read the exact version: open Accounts → Account Manager → New account and create the account below, with a long unique password.
dumbmonit@example.com
Allow the address DumbMonit connects from in Setup → XML API Service → Address Restrictions (Setup → XML API Management on MDaemon 26), then enter the account's full email address and its password.

To check more ports than SMTP, IMAP and webmail, set the Services option to a list like this one.
smtp,msa,imap,pop3,imaps,webmail

setup.title: Create a read-only API key for DumbMonit
steps: In the Meraki dashboard, open Organization → Settings and tick Enable access to the Cisco Meraki Dashboard API.

Open Organization → Administrators → Add admin and create an administrator dedicated to DumbMonit, with Organization access set to Read-only.
dumbmonit@example.com

In DumbMonit, enter api.meraki.com as the address and paste the key as API key. Leave Organization empty to read the first organization the key sees.

Organization access: Read-only

steps:
WinBox or WebFig → System → Users → Groups → Add: name the group as follows and tick only the policies listed below.
dumbmonit-read

System → Users → Add: create the user dumbmonit in that group, with a long random password.
dumbmonit
IP → Services: enable www-ssl and pick a certificate (create one under System → Certificates).

Optional, to hear about new RouterOS versions: System → Scheduler → Add, interval 1d, start time startup, with this On Event script.
/system package update check-for-updates once
In DumbMonit, enter the router's address (192.168.88.1) with that user name and password.

api

rest-api
Open the REST API under /rest

mc admin prometheus generate myminio cluster
Copy the value after bearer_token in the output: that is the token.

Prometheus token

use admin

setup.title: Monitor an MQTT broker
steps: In DumbMonit, enter the broker, for example broker.home.lan:1884 (port 1883 by default).
Tick Encrypted connection for a broker listening on 8883.
If the broker requires an account, fill in its user and password.
Optional: name a topic, to check that the account may still subscribe to it.
Optional: tick Expect a retained message only for a topic that carries one, typically an availability topic.

Subscribe (read) on the topic you name
Only if you name a topic

options.help: Topic the check subscribes to. Empty: it only connects, which already tells you the broker is alive and accepts your account.

label: SQL Server
summary: The database engine itself: databases that are not online, blocked requests, sessions against the limit, disk space of the data volumes, SQL Server Agent jobs and AlwaysOn availability groups.

setup.title: Create a read-only SQL Server login
steps:
Connect to the instance with SQL Server Management Studio or sqlcmd, with a login allowed to create logins, and create the login DumbMonit will use.
CREATE LOGIN dumbmonit WITH PASSWORD = 'choose-a-long-password', CHECK_POLICY = ON;
Check that the instance accepts SQL Server authentication (mixed mode) and listens on a fixed TCP port: SQL Server Configuration Manager, Network Configuration, TCP/IP.
In DumbMonit, enter the server address, for example sql.lan, or sql.lan:1444 for another port, then the login and its password.
Tick Accept an unverifiable certificate while the server still presents its self-signed certificate.
permissions:
VIEW SERVER STATE
Read sessions, requests and volumes

VIEW ANY DEFINITION
List the databases and their files

SQLAgentReaderRole (msdb)
Optional: read the Agent job history
setup.warning: Windows authentication is not supported: use a SQL Server login, on an instance that allows SQL Server authentication (mixed mode). Named instances need their fixed TCP port in the address.

In the mysql client, create an account with no privilege (adjust the host part to the DumbMonit machine).
CREATE USER 'dumbmonit'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'a-long-password';
In DumbMonit, enter the server, for example db.home.lan:3307 (port 3306 by default), then the account's user and password.
Optional: replace the default query SELECT 1 with one that returns a single number, to chart it.

Connect and run SELECT 1, nothing more

setup.title: Back up a device configuration
steps: Choose the device model in "Device model": it decides the commands sent, and nothing else is ever run on the device.
Create a read-only account on the device that may log in over SSH and show the running configuration.
For OPNsense through its API, create an API key for a user allowed to download backups; for PAN-OS, generate the API key of a read-only role.
The first SSH connection remembers the device's host key: if it ever changes, backups stop and an alert asks you to check it.

Only with an API profile (OPNsense API, PAN-OS)

permissions:
A read-only account
Allowed to log in over SSH and to show the configuration

On the Nextcloud server, set a random token with occ as the web server user (in Docker: docker exec -u www-data, then the container name).

summary: UPS served by Network UPS Tools: on battery, low or worn-out battery, charge, runtime left, load and input voltage, for every UPS the server publishes.
examples: Synology or QNAP NAS with a USB UPS

credentials.label: No authentication (recommended)
credentials.help: upsd lets any host it accepts read the UPS variables, without an account.

credentials.label: upsd user name / password
credentials.help: Sent with USERNAME and PASSWORD before reading. upsd does not check them to read; set them only if your setup asks for them.

fields.help: A user of upsd.users with no actions and no instcmds.

setup.title: Let DumbMonit read the NUT server
steps:
On a plain NUT install, add this line to upsd.conf and restart upsd.
LISTEN 0.0.0.0 3493
Open TCP port 3493 in the firewall for the DumbMonit host.
On a NAS, enable its network UPS server instead: Synology DSM → Control Panel → Hardware & Power → UPS, then add the DumbMonit host under Permitted DiskStation Devices.

Optional, to name this client: add a user without actions or instcmds to upsd.users, with a long random password, and restart upsd.
[dumbmonit]
password = a-long-random-password
In DumbMonit, enter the NUT server's address (nas.lan): every UPS it publishes is watched.
setup.warning: DumbMonit watches the UPS; it shuts nothing down: the machines it powers still need their own NUT client (upsmon) to shut down cleanly.

summary: Your cron job or backup script calls DumbMonit; when it goes quiet, you are told.

credentials.label: No authentication

setup.title: Make the job call in
steps: In the address, write a short label for the job, unique among your heartbeats: "nightly-backup".
Set the expected interval to the job's schedule ("24h" for a nightly job), or give a cron expression and a time zone, then save the monitor.

Copy the URL shown on the monitor page and call it at the end of the job.
curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 https://monit.example.com/api/push/<token>
To time the job, call .../start before it, then .../success or .../fail after it, with its output as the request body. Send an exit code as ?exit_code=2 or as .../2.
To report a failure at once, append ?status=down&msg=... to the URL.

ports.purpose: Heartbeat call (default port, 443 behind a proxy)

setup.warning: Call the URL at the end of the job, after the part that matters: a call at the top would report a success even when the job fails.

options.label: Expected interval
options.help: How often the job is supposed to call in: 30m, 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d (or a number of seconds). A missed call is declared once this interval plus the grace period has passed.

options.label: Grace period
options.help: Extra time tolerated after the expected interval before the heartbeat counts as missed: a percentage of the interval (10%) or a fixed duration (15m). Never less than one minute.

options.label: Cron schedule
options.help: Instead of the interval above: when the job is supposed to start, as a 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) or a shortcut such as @daily. Lists, ranges, steps and names are accepted: 30 2 * * *, */15 * * * *, 0 4 * * sun. Empty: use the interval.

options.label: Time zone
options.help: IANA time zone in which the cron schedule is read, for example Europe/Paris. It follows daylight saving time.

options.label: Maximum duration
options.help: A run that lasts longer than this raises the "job too long" alert: 30m, 2h. Needs a start call at the beginning of the job. Empty: a run still open after one period plus the grace period counts as stuck.

setup.title: Let DumbMonit read Traefik's API
steps:
Add these arguments to Traefik's command (or the same keys to its static configuration), then restart it.
--api.insecure=true
--metrics.prometheus=true
Open http://traefik.lan:8080/api/overview from the DumbMonit host: it must answer with JSON.

Optional: protect /api and /metrics with a basicAuth middleware on an entry point of your own, and create the user with htpasswd.
htpasswd -nbB dumbmonit 'a-long-password'
In DumbMonit, enter the Traefik host, for example traefik.lan, with the port of that entry point if it is not 8080.

setup.title: Create an API key for DumbMonit in TrueNAS
steps:
Open Credentials → Groups → Add, name the group as follows and give it the Local Administrator privilege.
dumbmonit

Open Credentials → Users → Add, name the account as follows and make dumbmonit its primary group. Leave shell access, sudo and SSH off.
dumbmonit
Open Credentials → Users → API Keys → Add, pick the dumbmonit user, name the key and copy it: TrueNAS shows it only once.
On TrueNAS 24.10, the path is the user menu at the top right → API Keys → Add.
In DumbMonit, enter the NAS address (for example nas.lan) and paste the key. Keep HTTPS.

The only privilege the REST API accepts for a key

options.help: Reads the last self-test of each disk. No test is ever started. TrueNAS 25.10 no longer offers this call; it is then skipped in silence.

options.label: Read TrueNAS's own alerts
options.help: Reads the alert list TrueNAS keeps itself — pool state, SMART, capacity, certificates, failed replications. Dismissed alerts are left out.

options.label: Watch the services

setup.title: Monitor a UDP service
steps: In the address, write the host and the UDP port: "192.168.1.20:5060". The port is required.
To check that the service really answers, fill in "Datagram to send" and "Expected reply".
Without an expected reply, the check only fails when the host answers that the port is closed.

ports.purpose: The service's UDP port, as written in the address (161 is only an example)

setup.warning: UDP has no connection: without an expected reply, a firewall that silently drops the datagrams looks healthy.

options.label: Port
options.help: Used if the address does not give one. There is no default: UDP has no standard port to fall back on.

options.label: Datagram to send
options.help: Sent as one datagram, 1400 bytes at most. In text, \n \r \t \0 \\ and \xNN are read as escapes. Empty: an empty datagram.

options.label: Datagram encoding
options.help: Text sends the characters as typed, Hex reads pairs of hexadecimal digits (spaces allowed).

options.label: Expected reply
options.help: Text the reply must contain. Empty: the check succeeds unless the host answers that the port is closed, and silence counts as success.

options.label: Allow loopback and link-local targets
options.help: By default the check refuses addresses only the DumbMonit host itself can reach (127.0.0.1, ::1, 169.254.x.x). Enable this to monitor a service running on the DumbMonit host. Private LAN addresses (10.x, 192.168.x) are always allowed.

ports.purpose: Only with an http:// address (default port)

setup.warning: Only the text the server sends is compared: pages drawn by JavaScript or behind a login are not followed.

options.label: Scope
options.help: Page: only the address above. Site: every page under the same folder, found through the site's sitemap or by following its links.

options.label: Max pages
options.help: Site scope only: pages read at most on each check, from 1 to 200.

options.label: Path prefix
options.help: Site scope only: follow only the pages whose path starts with this, for example /docs/. Empty: the folder of the address above.

options.label: Ignore lines
options.help: Regular expressions, one per line or joined with |: the text lines they match are left out of the comparison. For clocks, counters and "last updated" lines.

options.label: Watched area
options.help: Compare only the text inside these elements: a tag, #id, .class or [attribute=value], several separated by commas, for example main or #content. Empty, or not found on a page: the whole page.

options.label: Excluded areas
options.help: Leave the text of these elements out, same syntax: a cookie banner, a "latest posts" box, an ad slot. For example .cookie-banner, #sidebar.

options.label: Compare menus, header and footer

options.help: Site scope: addresses that differ only by their ?… part are one page. Tracking parameters (utm_…, fbclid, gclid…) are always left out.

setup.warning: Only what the server sends is read: for a page drawn by JavaScript, set "Blank page below" to 0.

options.label: Expected text
options.help: A phrase the page must show, such as your company name or "Add to cart". Case and spacing do not matter. Empty: not checked.

options.label: Blank page below (characters)
options.help: Visible text shorter than this counts as a blank page (20 by default, so short legitimate pages pass), from 0 to 100000. 0 turns the check off.

options.label: Max redirects
options.help: Redirects followed at most, from 0 to 30. Going from http to https or from example.com to www.example.com is normal and never an error; a loop or more redirects than this is.

options.label: Category
options.help: A label of your own (Shop, Blog, Client: Acme…), shown with the site and in its metrics. Set by the CSV import, which also guesses one (E-commerce, Blog, Web app, Showcase) when the page gives a clear sign. Empty: none.

options.label: User agent
options.help: Sent instead of DumbMonit's own, for a site that serves robots differently. Empty: DumbMonit/<version>.

options.label: Ignore query strings
options.help: Leave ?utm_source=… and other URL parameters out when comparing the final address and the canonical URL.

options.label: Check for changes every (minutes)
options.help: How often the title, description, canonical URL, final address and robots.txt are compared with the reference, from 0 to 10080 (a week). Up/down, blank page and expected text are checked at every polling interval regardless. A value seen once is confirmed at the next poll. Empty: the server default, 360 (DUMBMONIT_WEBSITE_CHANGE_CHECK_MINUTES). 0: at every poll.

options.label: Confirm a change after (checks)
options.help: A different title, description, canonical URL or other watched value is only reported once it was read this many times in a row, from 1 to 10. Keeps A/B tests and flaky caches quiet. Also applies to the sharp drop of the page text.

options.label: Near-empty page: text drop (%)
options.help: Reports a page whose visible text falls by more than this percentage below its usual size (a 200+ character reference is needed), from 0 to 99, confirmed like any change. Catches a page that is no longer blank but almost. 0 turns the check off.

options.label: Watch the final address
options.help: Report when, after its redirects, the site lands somewhere else (another host or path). http to https, www and trailing slashes never count.

options.label: Watch the title
options.help: Report a changed or missing <title>.

options.label: Watch the meta description
options.help: Report a changed or missing meta description.

options.label: Watch the canonical URL
options.help: Report a changed or missing canonical link.

options.label: Watch the robots directives
options.help: Report a changed robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag header (noindex, nofollow…).

options.label: Watch Open Graph
options.help: Report a changed og:title or og:description.

options.label: Watch the page language
options.help: Report a changed <html lang>.

options.label: Watch the h1 count
options.help: Report a different number of <h1> headings.

options.label: Watch hreflang
options.help: Report a changed set of hreflang language alternates.

options.label: Watch the Google verification tag
options.help: Report a changed or missing google-site-verification meta tag (losing it can cut access to Search Console).

options.label: Wait before the next request to this domain (seconds)
options.help: Minimum gap after this site's check before any other check of a site on the same domain (www.example.com and shop.example.com share one), from 0 to 3600. Keeps a firewall or CDN from mistaking a list of sites for an attack. Empty: the server default, 2 (DUMBMONIT_WEBSITE_HOST_SPACING_SECS).

options.label: Allow loopback and link-local targets
options.help: By default the check refuses addresses only the DumbMonit host itself can reach (127.0.0.1, ::1, 169.254.x.x). Enable this to monitor a service running on the DumbMonit host. Private LAN addresses (10.x, 192.168.x) are always allowed.

label: Windows (WinRM, no agent)
summary: A Windows server or PC without installing anything, through WinRM and WMI queries: CPU, memory, disks, services (the chosen ones and every automatic service that is stopped), uptime and recent event log errors.

credentials.label: Windows account
credentials.help: A local or domain account in the Remote Management Users group, as dumbmonit, DOMAIN\dumbmonit or dumbmonit@domain.

fields.label: User name
fields.help: The account created on the server, as dumbmonit (local) or DOMAIN\dumbmonit.

setup.title: Give DumbMonit a WinRM account on the Windows server
steps:
On the server, in an elevated PowerShell, enable WinRM.
Enable-PSRemoting -SkipNetworkProfileCheck -Force

Create the HTTPS listener with a certificate named after the server (use your own certificate instead of this self-signed one if you have one), then open its port.
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -DnsName "srv01.corp.example.com" -CertStoreLocation Cert:\LocalMachine\My
New-Item -Path WSMan:\LocalHost\Listener -Transport HTTPS -Address * -CertificateThumbPrint $cert.Thumbprint -Force
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "WinRM HTTPS" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 5986 -Action Allow

Create the account with a long random password, then add it to the groups listed below.
net user dumbmonit * /add
net localgroup "Remote Management Users" dumbmonit /add
net localgroup "Performance Monitor Users" dumbmonit /add
net localgroup "Event Log Readers" dumbmonit /add
Give the account access to the WMI namespace: wmimgmt.msc → right-click WMI Control → Properties → Security → Root → CIMV2 → Security, add it and tick Enable Account and Remote Enable.
In DumbMonit, enter the server name as its certificate names it (srv01.corp.example.com) and log in as dumbmonit, or DOMAIN\dumbmonit for a domain account.

Allows the WinRM login

Only for the event log counts

Reads the WMI classes
setup.warning: The account runs no command on the server, it only reads WMI. NTLM and Basic (HTTPS only) are supported, Kerberos is not. Pending Windows updates cannot be read this way. A self-signed certificate needs the option Accept an unverifiable certificate.

options.label: Allow unencrypted traffic
options.help: Use HTTP on port 5985 instead of HTTPS on port 5986. Not recommended: the server must allow unencrypted WinRM, and everything that crosses the network, the login included, can be read. Leave it off whenever an HTTPS listener exists.

options.label: Port
options.help: Used if the address does not give a port. 5986 for HTTPS, 5985 with unencrypted traffic.

options.label: Authentication
options.help: NTLM works with local and domain accounts. Basic must be enabled on the server and is only accepted over HTTPS. Kerberos is not supported.

options.label: Accept an unverifiable certificate
options.help: The device ships a self-signed certificate: enable this unless you installed one DumbMonit trusts.

options.label: Timeout per request (seconds)
options.help: Time allowed for each call, from 1 to 120.

options.label: Services to follow
options.help: Service names separated by commas. Each gets an up/down series, and one missing from the server counts as stopped. Every automatic service that is stopped is reported anyway.

options.label: Stopped services to ignore
options.help: Automatic services allowed to be stopped, separated by commas; a * at the start or the end is a wildcard. Updaters and delayed-start services such as gupdate are already ignored.

options.label: Event logs to count
options.help: Classic logs whose recent errors are counted (audit failures for Security), separated by commas. Write none to turn it off.

options.label: Event window (minutes)
options.help: Errors logged during this many minutes are counted, from 1 to 1440.

label: XCP-ng / XenServer
summary: An XCP-ng or XenServer pool through XAPI: hosts disabled or offline, VMs and their power state, storage repositories filling up, and a high-availability pool that can no longer survive the host failures it is set to tolerate.

credentials.label: User name and password
credentials.help: The dumbmonit account, registered on the pool as a subject with the read-only role.

fields.label: User name
fields.help: As the pool's directory knows it.

setup.title: Give DumbMonit a read-only XAPI account
steps:
On every host of the pool, create a local account with a long random password.
useradd -M -s /sbin/nologin dumbmonit
passwd dumbmonit

On the pool coordinator, turn on PAM authentication once.
xe pool-enable-external-auth auth-type=PAM service-name=pam

Register the account as a subject and note the UUID it prints.
xe subject-add subject-name=dumbmonit

Give that subject the built-in read-only role, with the UUID.
xe subject-role-add uuid=SUBJECT_UUID role-name=read-only
In DumbMonit, enter the address of the pool coordinator (for example xcp01.lan) with that user name and password.
permissions:
read-only role (XAPI)
Sees hosts, VMs, storage repositories and HA
setup.warning: If the pool already uses Active Directory, create the account there and skip steps 1 and 2. XCP-ng uses a self-signed certificate: enable "Accept an unverifiable certificate" unless the DumbMonit host trusts it.
